analysis.one_liner: Britannia Industries makes and sells packaged biscuits, cakes, rusk, bread and dairy products across India under brands like Britannia, Tiger, Good Day and Milk Bikis.
analysis.whats_happening: The stock hit a fresh 52-week low of ₹4,537.9 on 23 Oct 2026, down roughly 6.7% over six straight sessions amid broad market weakness. The board meets on 5 Nov 2026 to approve Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results - under two weeks from now - which should show whether the wholesale disruption from the September GST rate transition was a one-quarter blip and whether planned price hikes are protecting margins against rising input costs.
analysis.plain_terms: Britannia is one of India's best-run packaged food companies by the numbers - very high returns on capital - but the share price doesn't currently agree, sitting at a one-year low. The tension: Q1 FY27 profit grew 14% once a temporary GST-related pricing disruption faded, yet milk, fuel, palm oil and packaging costs are all rising together, and the market seems to be pricing in margin pressure ahead of price hikes management says are still coming. This isn't a stock-split or demerger story - it's a genuine decline in a richly valued stock amid cost worries.
analysis.quarters: Q4 FY26 (Mar quarter): sales up 7.1%, net profit up 21.6%, EBITDA margin 18.54%; full FY26 PAT was ₹2,537 crore, up 16.3%. Q1 FY27 (Jun quarter, reported 6 Aug 2026): revenue ~₹5,000 crore (+9.5% YoY), PAT ₹593 crore (+14% YoY), EBITDA margin expanded to 16.8% from 16.4%. Management said rural/wholesale demand was disrupted by a dual-pricing transition in April-May but recovered by June, and flagged sharp input inflation: milk +11%, industrial fuel +69%, laminate packaging +14%, with palm oil and sugar also up. They guided to defending FY27 EBITDA margins at FY26 levels via another 1.5-2% of pricing (on top of ~1% taken in Q1). The September quarter reportedly saw a fresh GST rate-transition disruption in wholesale buying - Q2 FY27 results (due 5 Nov 2026) will show whether that dented volumes materially; this is a timing/channel effect flagged by management, not an accounting restatement, but still worth watching for comparability.
analysis.performance_read: No recent corporate action (last split was in 2018) explains the 27.5% fall from the October 2024 peak of ₹6,258 - this is a genuine price decline, not a stock-mechanics illusion. Over 5 years, total return is +34.9%, slightly ahead of peer Nestle India (+32.9%) and ahead of the Nifty (+24.7%). But the more recent picture is weak: 3-year return is just +4.4% versus the Nifty's +18.2%, and over the last year the stock is down 24% versus the Nifty's 13% fall and Nestle's 6.7% fall - Britannia has underperformed both the market and its closest FMCG peer badly in the near term.
analysis.valuation_read: At the current price of ₹4,537.9, using FY26 EPS of ₹108.11, the trailing P/E works out to roughly 42x (P/B roughly 19x on a book value of ₹236.72) - lower than the ~46x P/E and ~21x P/B quoted by some data providers, which appear to reflect the price before the recent fall. It is cheap only relative to its own history and to some FMCG peers (one source put a peer median P/E near 72x) - not cheap in absolute terms. Whether it is 'cheap' depends on whether the market's current worry (margin compression from input costs) proves temporary or structural; the multiple still prices in a lot of sustained profitability.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently volume-assisted but margin-led: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 9.5% while profit grew faster (14%) as EBITDA margin expanded to 16.8%, meaning profit growth is outpacing the top line rather than simply tracking it. Management's own commentary ties near-term growth sustainability to further price hikes (1.5-2% more planned) rather than volume alone, given rising commodity costs - a margin-led growth phase, which in a cost-exposed food business can reverse quickly if pricing doesn't stick.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into cash well: FY26 operating cash flow of about ₹2,612 crore against capex of about ₹206 crore left free cash flow of roughly ₹2,406 crore, close to full conversion of net profit into cash. Non-current borrowings fell nearly 60% during FY26 (₹713 crore to ₹286 crore), leaving the balance sheet close to debt-free. The real risk here is business risk (commodity cost inflation squeezing margins), not financial risk (leverage or liquidity) - there is no debt-driven fragility in the picture.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Associated Biscuits International, part of the Wadia group) stood at about 50.6% as of June 2026, with the single largest promoter entity holding close to 44.8%. Promoter pledge is 0% as of both March and June 2026, formally confirmed by the promoter to the exchanges - a clean picture on that front. Institutional ownership is split between FIIs (~13.4%) and domestic mutual funds (~12.3%); no specific marquee individual investor was found on the register in available sources - not verified either way, check Screener's shareholding pattern for named individual holders.
strengths: FY26 ROCE of ~56% and ROE of ~54% - exceptional capital efficiency for a packaged food business
Near debt-free balance sheet: non-current borrowings cut by ~60% in FY26 (₹713 cr to ₹286 cr)
FY26 free cash flow of about ₹2,406 crore against capex of only ~₹206 crore - profits are largely converting to cash
Q1 FY27 profit growth (14%) outpaced revenue growth (9.5%) as EBITDA margin expanded to 16.8% despite input cost inflation
Zero promoter pledge and stable promoter holding (~50.6%)
watchpoints: Broad-based input cost inflation - milk +11%, industrial fuel +69%, laminate packaging +14%, plus rising palm oil and sugar costs - management says margins depend on another 1.5-2% of pricing still to come through
Stock at a fresh 52-week low, down 24% over one year, underperforming both the Nifty and peer Nestle India over 1 and 3 years
September 2026 wholesale disruption linked to a GST rate transition - Q2 FY27 results (due 5 Nov 2026) will show whether this was a one-quarter hit or a bigger demand issue
Recent CFO change (new CFO effective 1 Oct 2026) alongside a small (₹6.37 crore) GST demand notice under litigation - financially immaterial but worth tracking for continuity
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results on 5 Nov 2026 - specifically whether EBITDA margin held near FY26 levels despite input cost inflation, and whether the September GST-linked wholesale disruption was transient or a sign of deeper volume weakness.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 numbers (revenue ~₹5,000 cr, PAT ₹593 cr, EBITDA margin 16.8%) were cross-checked across multiple independent sources and are consistent. One source's FY26 free cash flow figure of ₹24,060 crore appears to be a formatting/decimal error and was discarded in favour of the cross-checked OCF-minus-capex figure of ~₹2,406 crore. Headline P/E (45.97x) and P/B (21x) from data providers appear to reflect a higher price point before the recent fall to a 52-week low; this report recomputes P/E (~42x) and P/B (~19x) using the verified last close of ₹4,537.9 against FY26 EPS/book value. Could not verify from available sources whether any specific named marquee investor holds a stake - flagged as not verified.
